(a) 
Subsection (a) of section 521 of title 38, United States Code, is amended to read as follows:


“(a) 
The Administrator shall pay to each veteran of World War I, World War II, the Korean conflict, or the Vietnam era, who meets the service requirements of this section, and who is permanently and totally disabled from non-service-connected disability not the result of the veteran’s willful misconduct or vicious habits, pension at the rate prescribed by tills section.”



 
    (b) Such section is further amended by amending subsection (g) to read as follows:


“(g) 
A veteran meets the service requirements of this section if he served in the active military, naval, or air service—

“(1) 
for ninety days or more during either World War I, World War II, the Korean conflict, or the Vietnam era;


“(2) 
during World War I, World War II, the Korean conflict, or the Vietnam era, and was discharged or released from such service for a service-connected disability;


“(3) 
for a period of ninety consecutive days or more and such period ended during World War I, or began or ended during World War II, the Korean conflict, or the Vietnam era; or


“(4) 
for an aggregate of ninety days or more in two or more separate periods of service during more than one period of war.”




 
    (c) The catchline of section 521 of title 38, United States Code, is amended to read as follows:



“§ 521. Veterans of World War I, World War II, the Korean conflict, or the Vietnam era”.




 
    (d) Subsection (a) of section 541 of title 38, United States Code, is amended to read as follows:


“(a) 
The Administrator shall pay to the widow of each veteran of World War I, World War II, the Korean conflict, or the Vietnam era who met the service requirements of section 521 of this title, or who at the time of his death was receiving (or entitled to receive) compensation or retirement pay for a service-connected disability, pension at the rate prescribed by this section.”



 
    (e) 
Paragraph (1) of subsection (e) of such section is amended to read as follows:


“(1) 
before (A) December 14, 1944, in the case of a widow of a World War I veteran, or (B) January 1, 1957, in the case of a widow of a World War II veteran, or (C) February 1, 1965, in the case of a widow of a Korean conflict veteran, or (D) before the expiration of ten years following termination of the Vietnam era in the case of a widow of a Vietnam era veteran; or”.



 
    (f) The catchline of section 541 of title 38, United States Code, is amended to read as follows:


“§541. Widows of World War I, World War II, Korean conflict, or Vietnam era veterans”.



 
    (g) 
Subsection (a) of section 542 of title 38, United States Code, is amended by striking out “or the Korean conflict” and inserting in lieu thereof “the Korean conflict, or the Vietnam era”.
 
    (h) 
The catchline of section 542 of title 38, United States Code, is amended to read as follows:



“§ 542. Children of World War I, World War II, Korean conflict, or Vietnam era veterans”.

fable.w: This section only amends veterans' pension eligibility to add Vietnam era veterans, their widows, and children, along with conforming changes to catchlines and tables. The tempting reading is that veterans and widows are outside parties interacting with the government, but they are merely benefit recipients, and benefit entitlements are expressly excluded from participation. There is no consultation, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue involved.
fable.s: The Administrator shall pay to each veteran of World War I, World War II, the Korean conflict, or the Vietnam era, who meets the service requirements of this section

qwen_block.w: This section establishes eligibility criteria and payment obligations for veterans' pensions. It does not require consultation, coordination, or input from outside parties (such as veterans, states, or the public) before the government makes a decision. The definition explicitly excludes applications for benefits or grants, and this text describes the statutory basis for such benefits rather than a participatory process.
qwen_block.s: The Administrator shall pay to each veteran of World War I, World War II, the Korean conflict, or the Vietnam era, who meets the service requirements of this section, and who is permanently and totally disabled from non-service-connected disability not the result of the veteran’s willful misconduct or vicious habits, pension at the rate prescribed by tills section.
qwen_block.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the section involves veterans (who are outside the federal government) receiving benefits, it constitutes participation. However, the definition explicitly excludes "applications for benefits or grants." This section merely defines eligibility criteria and payment obligations for pensions; it does not require the government to consult with veterans, hold public hearings, or form advisory boards with outside members before making decisions. The interaction is purely administrative (paying benefits based on statutory criteria), not participatory in the decision-making sense defined.

opus.w: This section only sets who qualifies for veterans' and widows' pensions and makes matching changes to headings and the table of sections. Getting a benefit is not participation under the definition. Nothing requires the Administrator to consult, hold hearings or take outside input before deciding anything, and the section gives no outside party a right to sue or object. The tempting reading treats veterans receiving pensions as people taking part in a decision, but they are only beneficiaries, not participants in federal decision-making.
opus.s: The Administrator shall pay to each veteran of World War I, World War II, the Korean conflict, or the Vietnam era, who meets the service requirements of this section
